# Parkinson's disease — surgical and device therapies

> 5 concept packs from the research run on surgical and device therapies (deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait); 94 of the family's 1,155 claims are grouped under this section in llms-facts.txt. Educational research reference, not medical advice.

## Concept packs

- [Run-level pack: Surgical and device therapies](https://llmsx.org/tree/parkinson-s-disease-surgical-and-device-therapies-deep-brain-stimulation-adaptive-dbs-focused-ultrasound-levodopa-pumps-and-infusions-and-neuromodulation-for-gait/): Run-level pack covering deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait
- [Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads](https://llmsx.org/tree/adaptive-closed-loop-dbs-and-directional-leads/): Personalized adaptive DBS showed benefits in a small feasibility trial, while another small beta-feedback trial found no significant advantage over continuous DBS
- [Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming](https://llmsx.org/tree/deep-brain-stimulation-stn-gpi-patient-selection-and-programming/): STN and GPi DBS selection depends on the patient’s disabling symptoms, levodopa response, neuropsychological risks and treatment goals
- [Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS](https://llmsx.org/tree/device-aided-therapies-compared-pumps-infusions-and-dbs/): Subcutaneous apomorphine and levodopa pumps, intestinal levodopa infusion and DBS differ in invasiveness, daily management and adverse effects
- [Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy](https://llmsx.org/tree/focused-ultrasound-thalamotomy-and-pallidotomy/): US target-specific approvals and NICE research-only recommendations need separate interpretation
- [Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms](https://llmsx.org/tree/spinal-cord-stimulation-tms-and-tdcs-for-gait-and-motor-symptoms/): Two blinded SCS trials did not establish gait benefit from the tested protocols

## Top sources, live-checked 2026-11-27

- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11875732 (5 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11875732/): Important burdens differ by modality: apomorphine can cause skin nodules, nausea and hypotension; intestinal levodopa can cause tube obstruction or displacement and abdominal complications
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426 (5 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/): For persistent stimulation-related adverse effects, the programming review recommends checking electrode location, reducing stimulation current and/or changing the active contact
- [cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie (5 claims in this run)](https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/): Both STN and GPi are effective motor-symptom targets; the CNS guideline supports either target for motor treatment rather than a universal target preference
- [nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3 (5 claims in this run)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3): The 2026 referral consensus states that pre-DBS assessments should include neurological
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11502575 (4 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11502575/): Daily device work matters in treatment choice: LCIG and apomorphine pumps require cartridge changes and handling, often with relative or nursing support
- [pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35791766 (4 claims in this run)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35791766/): Sources differ on unilateral focused ultrasound pallidotomy for Parkinson's disease
- [accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15 (4 claims in this run)](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S006D.pdf): Patient selection requires more than symptom severity: the tremor-dominant Parkinson’s prescriber information requires MRI suitability, ability to tolerate and communicate during treatment
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5822192 (3 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5822192/): Thalamotomy trial safety findings included two cases of mild hemiparesis from internal-capsule heating that improved, alongside persistent orofacial paresthesia, finger paresthesia and ataxia
